newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-LALIME KEEPS HIS SPOTLESS RECORD INTACT.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-LALIME KEEPS HIS SPOTLESS RECORD INTACT.

text.p: Stu Barnes' fluke goal in the third period broke a tie, and Patrick Lalime had 49 saves as the Pittsburgh Penguins brought their unbeaten streak to 14 games with a 4-2 victory over the Calgary Flames on Tuesday.
Lalime improved to 14-0-2 since he was recalled from the minors, extending his own record for the best career start by a goaltender.
He stopped 19 of 20 shots in the third period.
"I'm just trying to enjoy it," Lalime said. "I was used to facing a lot of shots when I was in the minors. It keeps you busy and keeps you ready ... sometimes that's good."
Kevin Hatcher, Ron Francis and Mario Lemieux also scored for the Penguins.
In Los Angeles, Dave Andreychuk had two first-period goals and Martin Brodeur stopped 32 shots as the New Jersey Devils snapped the Los Angeles Kings' five-game unbeaten streak with a 4-1 victory.
Bobby Holik added a goal and two assists and Scott Stevens set up two goals, including his 200th assist with the Devils.

In New York, Mark Messier's goal with 1:41 left in regulation lifted the New York Rangers into a 4-4 tie with the Edmonton Oilers, who have lost only once at Madison Square Garden in nearly seven years.
Ryan Smyth scored twice and ex-Ranger Doug Weight had three assists for Edmonton.
"We didn't play very well in the last five to six minutes of the hockey game. We started backing up instead of keeping it going," said Oilers coach Ron Low."
In Philadelphia, John LeClair scored at 9:23 of the third period to lift the Philadelphia Flyers into a 3-3 tie against the Dallas Stars in a matchup of first-place teams.

"Overall we didn't play as well as we would have liked to," LeClair said. "It's nice to come back and get a point out of this but when you look at the big picture, we didn't play as well as we could have. That part's disappointing."
Benoit Hogue had a goal and an assist for the Stars, who increased their lead in the Central Division to four points over second-place Detroit.

In Tampa Bay, Bill Houlder's wrist shot from the top of the right faceoff circle just over two minutes into overtime beat a screened Patrick Roy as the Tampa Bay Lightning rallied for a 3-2 victory over the Colorado Avalanche.
Houlder gathered in a loose puck and wristed it through traffic, beating Roy just inside the right post.
"I just skated in the gap and threw it on net," Houlder said. "I never scored an OT goal, not even in Pee Wee leagues."
